Change has been successfully rebased and submitted as e2fae4b9fe17e30149b077b38ea513d7207c5405
I don't think this is necessary.
It used to build `serialbridge` and its unit test since the default transport is null. So it will not build in CI test.
meson.build has been declared and can be used directly
Your interface doesn't have any methods, why create it at all?
Acked. I thought it was needed for `ipmid`, but actually it doesnot. Removed.
Hard-code is not a good choice. If the device parameter does not exist, we can exit directly.
Rather than having this file as a loose association of variables and functions, held together with a namespace, make it more c++-like and use a class.
rather than a uint8_t* and length, it might be more appropriate to use a std::span<uint8_t>
This is more of a coding for fun and learning new things, but the escaped/unescaped streams seem to be begging to be implemented with std::ranges transformations and/or filters.
It needs to add extra byte before the escaped byte. Transform might not be able to handle. Move to use `for_each` to iterate byte stream.

before pushing things into the buffer, make a call to buffer.reserve(data.size() + encoding_extras_size) where encoding_extras_size is the size of all the extra bytes added to frame the packet (this includes the escape chars). This will eliminate the need for a realloc and copy. Instead of looping through buffer twice to determine the number of characters that need to be escaped, it is reasonable to just use buffer.size() * 2 plus the other header/trailer bytes.

don't format the string and then log it, use lg2 as intended so it can log useful metadata as well:

```
lg2::info("Write serial request message with len={LEN}, netfn={NETFN}, "
          "lun={LUN}, cmd={CMD}, seq={SEQ}",
          "LEN", requestBuffer.size(), "NETFN", netfn, "LUN", lun,
          "CMD", cmd, "SEQ", seq);
```
No need for c_str() at all.
It seems need to use `c_str()`. Otherwise, it got a compiler error.
use lg2 for all output to make sure stuff gets appropriately logged.

don't format the string and then log it, use lg2 as intended so it can log useful metadata as well:

```
lg2::info("Read serial request message with len={LEN}, netfn={NETFN}, "
          "lun={LUN}, cmd={CMD}, seq={SEQ}",
          "LEN", requestBuffer.size(), "NETFN", netfn, "LUN", lun,
          "CMD", cmd, "SEQ", seq);
```
please use static constexpr for values like this in a header file instead of c-style #define

data should not be part of the 'header' struct.

Also, to ensure that your struct doesn't get word or dword aligned by the compiler, you might want to use ```__attribute__((packed))```

Rather than commenting this out, the best practice would be to find a way that the global variable is not needed. Often this means putting the variable in a class that allows access to the methods that need it and then putting an instance of that class on the stack at an appropriate level.
from my perusal of the code, serialchannel is not used outside of this file nor outside of this function, so you could declare it here and it can go out of scope when this function ends.
I don't think you need the .what() here. I though that lg2 could process std::exceptions internally.

why getUnescapedCharact with no er? Below is proccessEscapedCharacter.


```suggestion
uint8_t SerialChannel::getUnescapedCharacter(uint8_t c)
```
Acknowledged. Using `std::tie` since the response is `std::tuple`.
should be + 4; need bmStart, bmStop and two checksums
this can throw, you should probably catch its errors and report like the other errors. Maybe just move it up into the previous try/catch block
is there a reason for ignoring exceptions here? It seems that you would want to report them. Maybe by writing an error response back the the serial caller?
Exception is captured in `write` function. Also adding return code for capture error.
Please don't put using lines in the header file; put them in the cpp file to minimize namespace pollution.

ctx_state only has two values inProgress or idle; it might make sense to treat this as a bool with a name that has meaning:

```suggestion
    bool ctxMsgInProgress;
```
Acknowledged. Combine them into a three-state enum.

this is used as a bool in the code, so just make it a bool here. Also variables should be lowerCamelCase.

bool ctx
```suggestion
    bool ctxEscape;
```
Acknowledged. Combine them into a three-state enum.

I don't know how this is going to work with CI going forward.  I think we need some changes here.

I get that we're adding a provider here where we previously created them as separate repositories, and we now have the option to migrate the other implementations here.  That's good.

The way this is written though, we end up with none of the code being tested in CI.  This is bad.

Generally we require meson.options to be written where everything is enabled by default, so we get fully compile / unit-testing in CI and then the PACKAGECONFIG in Yocto removes it.  Please revisit this.

Each transport interface could add in [1]. CI will enable `tests` options that will compile and unit-test all the transport interface by default. If this doesn't fit the requirement, then I can revisit this.

[1] https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-host-ipmid/blob/master/meson.build#L348
The daemons are still not going to be compiled, are they?

The daemon will be compiled and unit-test will be executed against transport interface meson[1] for CI.

[1] https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-host-ipmid/blob/master/transport/serialbridge/meson.build
